notes: Class A conclusion: comprehensive scan of ALL 122 ingredients_text_he vs ingredients_raw_he pairs found ZERO confirmed BSIP1 over-trim truncation bugs. An initial automated diff surfaced 10 candidates across two refinement passes; every one was manually verified as a false positive caused by scrape-artifact noise (stray literal 'n' from lost newlines, mid-word stray spaces, mid-list allergen parentheticals) -- in each case ALL real ingredient/allergen content was correctly preserved in ingredients_text_he.

The single known suspect case (7290116936581, 'GO 20g protein') is NOT a trim bug: both the BSIP1 ingredients_raw_he AND the true upstream BSIP0 scrape (run_yogurt_task515_20260705T062308_corpus.json) agree the source page declared only 'חלב'. This is a source-data implausibility (physically impossible protein density from milk alone), reclassified and carried in the ledger under its own key.

3 products have ingredients_text_he correctly nulled per the missing_data_discard_rule (raw was marketing prose or near-empty scrape junk, not a real ingredient declaration) -- these are NOT trim bugs, but they DO feed the confirmed Class B null-ingredients-bestcase pattern.

Class B (null->best-case) is the dominant, confirmed issue class: 20 barcodes where a null macro field (ingredients/sugar/fat) maps to a top-of-range sub-score. Zero null-protein cases exist in the corpus (0/122) so the hypothesized protein_quality best-case pattern does not occur here.
Class C: 3 confirmed exact-duplicate pairs (byte-identical per-100g panels under different barcodes) + 1 near-duplicate pair flagged for human judgment (43944/45771, differs only by 0.2g sat-fat).

Class D: 1 CONFIRMED-impact contamination case (7290014758117, diabetes-association seal text) with hard trace evidence of a 2.2-point / full-letter-grade divergence vs its clean twin (57132). 27 lower-risk 'מאפיינים נוספים' header-bleed cases (hygiene debt, no confirmed score movement found in this pass). 8 kashrut-substitution mentions were correctly ruled OUT as false positives (legitimate ingredient-swap declarations, not contamination) after inspection.

Guard-flip finding: the drinkable pool's sugar shelf-relative IQR guard is CURRENTLY FAILING (scale=1.85 < 3.0 threshold, per the live run_record.json) even before any remediation. Applying the recommended Class B/C actions to drinkable (drops 6664655, 7290116932774, 7290116934228; n: 23->20) FIXES it (scale recomputes to 3.11, guard_scale_pass flips false->true) -- but lands drinkable exactly at the min_n=20 floor with zero margin for any further discard. Spoonable's guard was already passing and remains passing after remediation (n: 94->74, scale unchanged at 4.6).

compute_shelf_stats() was imported directly from the live score_engine.py (read-only call, no edits) to avoid reimplementing the IQR/MAD scale formula by hand; before-values reproduce run_record.json's published 4.6 (spoonable) / 1.85 (drinkable) exactly, confirming the method match.
